# Phase 01.1 Plan 06: Venue Namespace + SC4 Contrast Guardrail Summary

**The D-14 token boundary built as a hex-only, Cena-ramp-free `--venue-*` contract mapped through `@theme inline`, a total resolver that structurally cannot return a sub-AA token set, and two tripwires — a 20-pair contrast sweep with four oracle pins asserted first and a namespace/hex/dark-mechanism scan — 50 new cases, all observed failing before being committed green.**

## Performance

- **Duration:** 17 min
- **Started:** 2026-08-04T23:41:00Z
- **Completed:** 2026-08-04T23:58:00Z
- **Tasks:** 3
- **Files modified:** 5 (4 created, 1 modified)

## Accomplishments

- **SC4 is now proven rather than claimed.** Twenty real co-occurrence pairs are measured against non-uniform thresholds on every test run, and the palette is read out of `app/tokens/cena.css` as data — so a hex edited in the stylesheet is measured by the gate rather than ignored by it. The design project's contrast card proved this by hand; it is now a regression guard that runs in 3ms.
- **The guardrail has been observed refusing four different ways** — an incomplete table, a degraded palette value, a leaked ramp identifier, and a device-preference selector — each with a message naming the offender, the file and the measured value. A guardrail that has never refused anything is untested.
- **The D-14 boundary exists and is greppable.** `--venue-*` carries literal six-digit hex only, contains no Cena ramp identifier, and has **no v1 consumer** by design. Retrofitting it later would have meant re-cutting every token consumer; doing it now cost one file.
- **`resolveVenueTheme` makes AA a property of the type.** There is no way to obtain a `VenueTokens` value without having cleared every threshold — no `validate()` a caller can forget, which matters because the thing they would be forgetting is a legal accessibility gate.
- **Nothing regressed.** 663 baseline tests still pass; 713 total across 57 files; `tsc --noEmit` and `pnpm build` both exit 0. No file under `components/ui/` was touched (plan 01.1-07 owns those concurrently).

## Tripwire Failure Evidence

Four deliberate breaks, each observed red and reverted. `git status` after each revert showed only the intended new file.

**1. Incomplete sweep table** — `CONTRAST_PAIRS` truncated to its first 3 entries. Three tests went red:

> `AssertionError: CONTRAST_PAIRS has 3 entries. The sweep is the whole of SC4's proof; below 8 rows it is not a sweep, it is a sample.: expected 3 to be greater than or equal to 8`
>
> `AssertionError: No 3.0 (SC 1.4.11 non-text) row in CONTRAST_PAIRS — applying 4.5 to a border is a false failure, and this table must keep the distinction.`
>
> `AssertionError: DINE-04 last-good banner pair is missing from the sweep.: expected [ 'ink-body/paper', 'ink/paper', …(1) ] to include 'warning-ink/warning-soft'`

The identity-pinned control is what caught the missing release gate — the length guard alone would have passed at 8 rows with both gates deleted.

**2. Degraded palette value** — `--cena-ink-muted` changed from `#526260` to `#8a9a98` in `app/tokens/cena.css`. Three sweep rows refused:

> `SC4 VIOLATION — --cena-ink-muted (#8a9a98) on --cena-surface-chip (#dce4e3) measures 2.271:1, below the 4.5:1 floor. Renders at: Allergen chips (DINE-06) — the historic worst pair in the system. FIX THE VALUE, NOT THE THRESHOLD …`

This is the important one: it proves the sweep reads the **live stylesheet**, not a parallel copy of it, so the gate cannot be bypassed by editing the palette.

**3. Leaked ramp identifier** — `--venue-accent` changed to `var(--szeged-700)`. Two tests went red, from two different angles:

> `TOKEN BOUNDARY VIOLATION — app/tokens/venue.css references the Cena ramp identifier(s) --szeged-700. A raw ramp name can NEVER be re-mapped by a theme …`
>
> `TOKEN BOUNDARY VIOLATION — --venue-accent is "var(--szeged-700)", which is not strict #rrggbb …`

**4. Device-preference selector + disabled dark variant** — a `prefers-color-scheme` block appended to `venue.css` and the `@custom-variant` line commented out in `globals.css`:

> `D-10 VIOLATION — app/tokens/venue.css keys a media query on the device's colour scheme. Auto-darkening silently invalidates every ratio tests/theme/venue-contrast-guardrail.test.ts measures …`

**This probe found a real defect in my own test** — see Deviations, item 3. The dark-mechanism assertion initially passed over a commented-out declaration.

## Decisions Made

1. **The `declarations()` extractor was widened by one character.** `tests/lib/theme-width-scale.test.ts`'s key class is `[a-z0-9]+`, which cannot express a compound key. Copied verbatim it captures **5 of 16** Cena tokens and **5 of 7** venue tokens — and the two venue tokens it drops are `accent-ink` and `muted-ink`, the two *derived ink values* whose legibility is the entire point of the guardrail. Both copies use `[a-z0-9-]+` with an in-file note recording the divergence and why. The original is untouched (it is not in this plan's `files_modified`, and its own namespaces are single-word).
2. **`CONTRAST_PAIRS` carries 20 entries, not 18.** UI-SPEC rows 15 and 18 each name two backgrounds; flattening them into one entry per measured pair keeps the failure message unambiguous and stops a second measurement hiding inside a row. The UI-SPEC's own "22 evaluated pairs" line already acknowledges the row count is not the pair count.
3. **`VenuePolarity` is a single-member union.** The plan's input sketch includes "paper/ink polarity", but honouring it fully requires a dark surface triple, and 01.1-05 established (with a measured 2.36:1) that inventing one is threat **T-01.1-25**. Rather than invent hexes or drop the input silently, the type admits exactly `"light"` today and the module header states the three gated steps to add `"dark"` — widen the union, add the surface triple, add the dark core pairs to the sweep, **in that order**. Nothing is invented and nothing is hidden.
4. **Status pairs and the worst-case pair are pinned by identity, not just by count.** A separate control test asserts `warning-ink/warning-soft`, `danger/paper` and `ink-muted/surface-chip` are present. Deleting a release-gate row is the specific way a sweep gets quietly weakened, and a length guard does not catch it.
5. **The exempt row is asserted exempt, and still asserted resolvable.** `--cena-rule` measures 1.29 and is allowed to; the test asserts its `threshold` is `null` and that both tokens still resolve to hex. An exemption is not a licence to stop resolving the pair.
6. **Comment handling is direction-dependent, and that is now written down.** Plan 01.1-05 decided its SC1 source scan does **not** except comments (a commented-out external asset is one uncomment from shipping). This plan's dark-mechanism assertion needed the **opposite** rule, because a commented-out declaration is a dead mechanism. Both files now carry the reasoning so the next author does not "fix" one to match the other.

## Deviations from Plan

### Auto-fixed Issues

**1. [Rule 3 — Blocking] The `declarations()` extractor could not express this plan's token keys**

- **Found during:** Task 2
- **Issue:** The plan directs both tests to reuse `declarations(css, namespace)` from `tests/lib/theme-width-scale.test.ts` **verbatim**. Its key class is `[a-z0-9]+`, so `--cena-ink-body`, `--cena-surface-sunken`, `--cena-warning-border` and eleven others do not match at all. The verbatim copy extracts 5 of 16 Cena tokens — below the plan's own `>= 16` non-vacuity guard, so the sweep could not have run.
- **Fix:** `[a-z0-9-]+` in both copies, with a header note naming the one-character divergence and stating exactly which tokens the narrower class drops.
- **Files modified:** `tests/theme/venue-contrast-guardrail.test.ts`, `tests/theme/token-boundary.test.ts`
- **Verification:** Palette extraction guard passes at 16; venue extraction guard passes at 7; every `CONTRAST_PAIRS` token resolves (the `hex()` helper throws by name otherwise).
- **Committed in:** `e6bf057`, `3b3d1b6`

**2. [Rule 2 — Missing Critical] The two font slots needed a namespace that keeps "every `--venue-*` is a colour" true**

- **Found during:** Task 1
- **Issue:** The plan lists `--font-venue-display` / `--font-venue-body` among the nine venue tokens, and separately requires that every `--venue-*` value be strict six-digit hex. A font family is not a hex, so a slot named `--venue-font-display` would have made the hex rule unenforceable — the boundary test would have had to carry an exception list, and exception lists are where guardrails go to die.
- **Fix:** The slots are namespaced `--font-venue-*` (as the plan itself names them), which places them outside the `--venue-*` extraction entirely. The hex rule is therefore total over its namespace with no exceptions, and this is recorded in the test.
- **Files modified:** `app/tokens/venue.css`, `tests/theme/token-boundary.test.ts`
- **Verification:** `declarations(VENUE_CSS, "venue")` returns exactly the 7 colour tokens; all nine names present per the acceptance grep.
- **Committed in:** `49d3801`, `3b3d1b6`

**3. [Rule 1 — Bug] The dark-mechanism assertion passed over a commented-out declaration**

- **Found during:** Task 3's deliberate break
- **Issue:** The first version matched `/@custom-variant\s+dark\s*\(&:is\(\.dark\s+\*\)\)/` anywhere in the file. Commenting the declaration out in `app/globals.css` left the test **green** — the exact failure the assertion exists to prevent (a file that has lost dark support while looking like it has it). Found only because the plan required observing the test red.
- **Fix:** Anchored to line start with the `m` flag and a required trailing `;`, so a `/*`-prefixed line cannot satisfy it. In-file comment records both the defect and the deliberate contrast with the SC1 source scan's opposite comment policy.
- **Files modified:** `tests/theme/token-boundary.test.ts`
- **Verification:** Re-ran the same probe; the assertion now fails with its offender-naming message. Reverted; green.
- **Committed in:** `3b3d1b6`

**Impact on plan:** All three are inside this plan's own files. No scope creep, no architectural change, no Rule 4 escalation.

## Surfaced, Not Silently Resolved

- **The plan's `<verification>` block names "five files: oracle, no-third-party-assets, build-assets, touch-targets, guardrail, boundary" — that list has six entries.** `tests/theme/` now holds six files and 103 cases pass together with `theme-width-scale`. Reported rather than silently reconciled.
- **`01.1-UI-SPEC.md` remains unsigned** (`## Checker Sign-Off` all unchecked, `**Approval:** pending`), and this plan consumed its Color, Contrast Guardrail and Token Namespace sections verbatim. A later sign-off that changes a ramp value lands here first — though harmlessly, because the sweep reads the stylesheet rather than a copy, so a changed hex is *measured* rather than silently accepted.
- **The dark ramp is still owed.** 01.1-05's Known Stub said "plan 01.1-06 must add the dark core pairs to the contrast sweep before any dark surface is wired." That remains correct and remains **not done**, because the ramp is still not retrievable — no value was invented to close it. The sweep is now the place those rows go, and `VenuePolarity` is the place the polarity goes. Already recorded as `.planning/WINDOWS.md` entry 4; **no new ledger entry was added**, because this is the same defect, and `WINDOWS.md` is a shared file a concurrent worktree agent may also be writing.

## Known Stubs

None. The venue namespace having **no v1 consumer** is D-14's deliberate design, not a stub — v1 ships one brand on every surface (D-02 revised), and the contract is built now so the theming milestone grows the sweep by adding rows rather than inventing the mechanism under time pressure. Nothing renders an empty value, and nothing displays a placeholder.

## Issues Encountered

- **Tailwind v4 and an `@import`-ed `@theme inline` block.** Plan 01.1-05's finding A1 proved Tailwind processes `:root` declarations reached by `@import`; whether a full `@theme` block survives the same path was untested. It does — verified by build output, not assumed. Had it not, the fallback was to move the `@theme inline` block into `globals.css` and keep only `:root` in `venue.css`.
- **No blockers.** No auth gate, no checkpoint, no architectural decision.

## User Setup Required

None.

## Next Phase Readiness

**Ready.**

- **For the primitive and surface waves:** nothing here changes a rendered pixel. `--venue-*` has no consumer, and `app/globals.css` gained exactly one import line — the spacing scale and both width shields are byte-identical, so `tests/lib/theme-width-scale.test.ts` keeps its meaning.
- **For any wave that touches a colour:** `tests/theme/venue-contrast-guardrail.test.ts` is now a live gate on the Cena ramp. A re-skin that edits `app/tokens/cena.css` gets measured automatically, and the failure message names the token, both hexes, the surface and the threshold.
- **For Phase 4 (the diner surface):** `resolveVenueTheme` is the only sanctioned way to produce a token set, its header records the write-path (Server Action + Zod `superRefine`, never client-only) and injection (`style` prop on the root Server Component, never `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, never middleware, never a client fetch) rules, and the strict-hex constraint is enforced by test at the source.
- **For the theming milestone:** the growth path is additive — add a `next/font` instance and a `VENUE_FONT_PAIRINGS` member for a pairing; add `"dark"` to `VenuePolarity`, a surface triple, and the dark core pairs to `CONTRAST_PAIRS`, in that order.
